interactions.summary: Jiang reframes the second half of the seminar as teacher-training: everyone should leave able to teach Inferno to someone they love, using compare-and-contrast and other pedagogical techniques to expand imagination rather than merely decode literary meaning.
The seminar appears to close and then immediately restart with a clipped transition.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Likely room closeout with Jiang resuming

speaker_notes.note: The ending is heavily garbled and likely straddles a stop-and-start in the live seminar, but Jiang's pedagogical intent is still clear.

claims.claim: Jiang wants the seminar participants to leave not just understanding Inferno but able to teach it to students, friends, children, or parents.
The second half of the seminar will focus less on literary interpretation and more on techniques that expand imagination and help participants teach others.
Jiang treats compare-and-contrast as one of the most effective tools for making punishments, politics, and other infernal structures teachable.
By this point Jiang thinks the hardest interpretive work was Paradise, so Inferno should now be simple enough to support more active student contribution.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang's real goal is not private comprehension but transmissible understanding: leave and teach someone you love.
signature_moments.source_phrase: teaching it to someone that you love
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It condenses the seminar's public ethic and should survive into the episode read.
